routes.label: Check the domain before combining logarithms

question:
If all the logarithms are real numbers, the equality

\[ \begin{aligned} \log(x+3)+\log(x-1)\\ =\log(x^2-2x-3) \end{aligned} \]

is satisfied for:
solution:
Every argument of a real logarithm must be positive. The two logarithms on the left require \(x+3>0\) and \(x-1>0\), so \(x>1\). The right-hand argument factors as
\[
x^2-2x-3=(x-3)(x+1).
\]
For \(x>1\), the factor \(x+1\) is positive, so the right-hand logarithm also requires \(x>3\). This is the common domain.

On this domain, the product rule gives
\[
\log\bigl((x+3)(x-1)\bigr)
=\log(x^2-2x-3).
\]
Equal logarithms with the same valid base have equal arguments. Thus
\[
x^2+2x-3=x^2-2x-3,
\]
which reduces to \(4x=0\), or \(x=0\). This candidate violates \(x>3\), so it cannot satisfy the original equation. There are \(\boxed{\text{no real solutions}}\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
